resources.string: The battery HAL/healthd sees no battery: check the fuel gauge driver (power_supply \"battery\" node) and the health HAL.
The fuel gauge does not export voltage_now, or the health HAL cannot read it.
Looks like µV where Android expects mV: the health HAL does not scale voltage_now.
Looks like volts where Android expects mV: the health HAL scale is wrong.
Outside 3.0–4.6 V for a Li-ion cell: wrong scale or a fuel gauge problem.
Temperature is exactly 0: the battery thermistor is not read (missing temp node or wrong ADC channel).
Implausible temperature: wrong scale or thermistor channel.
The battery is hot; charging may be throttled. Repeat after it cools down.
CURRENT_NOW is not available: the fuel gauge does not export current_now or healthd does not read it. Charge speed cannot be measured.
The value looks like mA where Android expects µA (a phone with the screen on draws more than 20 mA): the driver or health HAL uses the wrong unit.
The sign is opposite to the AOSP convention (positive = charging). Common on Qualcomm gauges; apps may show charging as discharging.
The value did not change in 3 s; some gauges update slowly. Watch the live chart.
Plug in a charger and run again, or use the live charging test below.
A charger is detected but the battery does not charge: charger IC configuration, input current limit (AICL) or a temperature limit. Check the usb power_supply values.
The fuel gauge reports less than 70 per cent of the design capacity: a worn battery or a wrong learned capacity.
The health HAL reports a fault (temperature, voltage or failure).
charge_full / charge_full_design are not readable on this ROM.
/sys/class/power_supply is empty or not readable by apps (SELinux).
Plug in a charger: the test passes by itself when real charging current is seen. Then answer the questions.
With the usual charger, is charging as fast as expected?
Does it charge from a PC USB port?
